sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, a negatively tilted shortwave trough -- now apparent in moisture-channel imagery from the Dakotas to near MKC -- is expected to continue weakening gradually as it moves to the upper Mississippi Valley through the rest of the period. Southwesterly flow aloft will strengthen over parts of the interior Northwest, Great Basin and northern Rockies regions, ahead of an amplifying and slowly progressive near-coastal trough. A southern-stream perturbation -- currently evident over AZ -- is expected to move northeastward to the central/southern Rockies by 00Z, then across the central High Plains overnight. A strong vorticity maximum emanating from the base of this feature after 00Z in some models is related to convective feedback, though convectively induced vorticity augmentation/MCV development eventually is possible with the activity discussed in the southern slight-risk outlook section below. Finally, remnants of Alberto are forecast to eject north-northeastward to Lake Huron through the period, while gradually weakening. sections.title: Southeastern CO, TX/OK Panhandles to OK
sections.text: Widely scattered thunderstorms should develop in a regime of favorable diurnal heating of higher terrain, and low-level upslope flow, in the vicinity of the Raton Mesa and its eastward extension through Black Mesa. Activity will be high-based early in its life cycle, atop deeply mixed subcloud layers suitable for maintenance of both hail and severe gusts to surface. Forecast vertical shear will be favorable for supercellular organization, with effective-shear magnitudes in the 45-55-kt range. Very steep low/middle-level lapse rates are forecast amidst increasing moisture with eastward extent and with time, as the boundary layer at lower elevations recovers with the northward retreat of the outflow boundary. MLCAPE will increase eastward along the projected track of the convection into early evening as it encounters greater boundary-layer moisture, with 60s F surface dew points contributing to 2500-3000 J/kg values. Buoyancy will then decrease with eastward extent across north- central OK into the Ozarks, but gradually. sections.title: Northern Rockies region
sections.text: Widely scattered to scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop this afternoon within a broad regime of steep low/middle-level lapse rates -- augmented by diurnal heating of higher terrain -- and favorable low-level moisture. Strong upper-level flow and favorable cloud-layer shear will support organization of outflow-dominant multicellular clusters and perhaps bowing segments, primarily offering a damaging-wind threat. Isolated severe hail also possible.

sections.title: OH Valley/Lower MI
sections.text: Isolated damaging gusts are possible over the outlook area, and a tornado cannot be ruled out. The remnants of Alberto are well-defined this morning with a center of low/middle-level circulation still quite evident around EVV, moving north- northeastward. Progs reasonably show a pronounced CAPE void around the core region of this vortex throughout the day, related to clouds, precip, and poor deep-layer lapse rates. Away from that core region, primarily north through east of center, a sector of favorable diabatic heating, rich low-level moisture and related boundary-layer destabilization is expected, with cloud breaks evident in IR and early VIS imagery. Coverage and longevity of storms in this regime are in doubt, but marginally favorable CAPE-shear parameter spaces are evident to support some storm organization, including at least transient supercell characteristics. However, given the overall continued weakening of the circulation envelope, and resultant curved but small hodographs, the overall severe potential appears marginal. ..Edwards/Smith.. 05/30/2018

outlooks.summary: The most concentrated severe-weather threat appears to be across parts of Oklahoma and southern Kansas this evening and tonight, with damaging wind gusts expected. Other strong thunderstorm wind gusts will be possible from the northern Great Basin into the northern Rockies this afternoon and evening.

sections.title: Northern Great Basin into the northern Rockies
sections.text: Occasional thunderstorms are continuing within the southwesterly flow aloft in advance of short-wave trough lifting northeastward across northern California at this time. Area soundings exhibit moderately steep lapse rates and sufficient moisture with PW values near 0.75 inch. With the likelihood of stronger diabatic heating occurring on the lateral edges of a cloud band extending from northeast Nevada into extreme southwest Montana, the air mass will destabilize with MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg. Additional storms are expected to develop by early afternoon and spread northeastward within the deep layer southwest flow aloft. Deep-layer vertical shear will be enhanced by 35-45 kt mid-level winds suggesting a few strong-to-severe storms will be possible this afternoon and evening. The primary threat is expected to be severe wind gusts although isolated hail will also be possible with stronger cores.

sections.title: Upper Ohio Valley into the Great Lakes
sections.text: The remnant cyclonic circulation from Alberto remains well-defined in satellite imagery as the system moves northeastward over southwest Indiana. A band of strong low-level winds within the eastern periphery of the circulation is sampled by WSR-88D VAD wind profiles and is associated with strong low-level shear/SRH. The downstream instability is tempered by continuing warm mid-level temperatures, but diabatic heating is occurring in areas from northern Indiana into northwest Ohio and there is potential for several bands of convection to develop this afternoon and spread to the north or northeast. A threat for isolated tornadoes or strong wind gusts will continue into the evening. ..Weiss/Squitieri/Cook.. 05/30/2018

outlooks.summary: Severe weather risk remains evident across parts of Oklahoma and southern Kansas this evening and tonight, with damaging wind gusts expected. Other strong thunderstorm wind gusts are expected to develop from the northern Great Basin into the northern Rockies this afternoon and evening.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Forecast reasoning from prior outlooks remains on track, with convection evolving this afternoon in a manner largely as expected thus far. Primary changes to the outlook include a slight eastward extension of probabilities into southwest Missouri, as some hints exist that convection crossing parts of Oklahoma and Kansas overnight may remain organized a bit longer -- and thus persist a bit farther east, as well as a northward extension of low probabilities into northeast Montana as storms crossing southern Saskatchewan have expanded a bit southward across the international border. Otherwise, only minor line adjustments are being made to the prior outlook. ..Goss.. 05/30/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1128 AM CDT Wed May 30 2018/ ...Southeast Colorado/northwest Texas into southern Kansas and northern Oklahoma... outlooks.summary: Severe weather threat will persist across parts of Oklahoma and southern Kansas this evening and tonight, with damaging wind gusts expected. Isolated severe hail and/or damaging wind gusts also remains possible from the northern Great Basin into the northern Rockies and over Lower Michigan.

sections.title: 01Z Update
sections.text: ...Southeast CO eastward into southern KS/northern OK... Upscale growth into a well-organized MCS is still anticipated with the storms currently moving through far southeast CO and adjacent portion of the western OK Panhandle. Downstream airmass across the central/eastern Panhandles and western OK is characterized by temperatures in the 90s, mid 60s dewpoints and strong instability. Some increase in the convective inhibition is likely before the linear MCS moves into this area. However, the anticipated organized nature of the MCS as well as an increase in the moist inflow, resulting from a strengthening low-level jet, should easily overcome the convective inhibition. Current thinking is that the MCS will track along the KS/OK border with the southern extent close to the latitude of the OKC metro.

sections.title: Northern Great Basin into the northern Rockies
sections.text: A few storms capable of strong wind gusts and/or hail will remain possible during the next few hours as a shortwave trough continues to move through the Pacific Northwest.

sections.title: Lower MI
sections.text: 00Z DTX sounding sampled a PW of 1.85 inches, which is near-record moisture based on SPC sounding climatology. This very moist and modestly unstable airmass will continue to support a band of thunderstorms arcing across the central portions of Lower MI. A few damaging wind gusts have been reported over the last hour and the threat for isolated damaging winds will continue for the next hour or so until the band reaches the cooler, less moist, and less unstable air across northern portions of Lower MI. ..Mosier.. 05/31/2018

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms are developing across the region, with more widespread coverage expected. A WW may be necessary sometime later this afternoon, especially for southeast Colorado and far northeast New Mexico.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated convection has recently initiated off the higher terrain of the Colorado Front Range, with further intensification and greater areal coverage expected. Surface dewpoints have been slowly increasing into the lower 50s F across the region over the past few hours, beneath relatively steep lapse rates within a deep layer of the atmosphere (i.e 7.5-8.6 C/km from 1-6km). As such, modest instability (approximately 500 J/kg) is present across the area and is expected to increase throughout the afternoon in tandem with the diurnal cycle. While 35-45 kts of bulk shear supports some storm organization, particularly in southern Colorado, meager low-level shear suggests that most storms will become outflow dominant, especially in northern regions of the discussion area. As convective coverage gradually increases, some upscale growth in the form of linear clusters should occur (as suggested by recent high-resolution model guidance). One or more MCSs may be possible, especially in southeastern Colorado into far northeast New Mexico, where stronger mid-level flow and bulk shear are currently in place. As such, a severe thunderstorm watch may eventually be needed (particularly in southeastern Colorado/northeast New Mexico) pending convective trends.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Widely scattered strong thunderstorms, perhaps an isolated supercell or two, appear increasingly possible through 5-6 PM MDT. Severe weather potential is expected to remain marginal/isolated enough that a watch is not currently anticipated, but trends will continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Large-scale mid/upper support for convective development remains unclear. However, thunderstorm activity is in the process of increasing in response to sufficient diurnal boundary layer destabilization and orographic forcing across the Bitterroot Mountains vicinity, and along the higher terrain east through south of the upper Snake Valley. CAPE appears generally weak, which may remain a limiting factor to a more substantive severe weather threat, but lower/mid tropospheric lapse rates are becoming at least modestly steep. Although this is generally south of a belt of 50 kt southwesterly 500 mb crossing central Idaho and western Montana, in the wake of a significant short wave trough shifting northeastward through Alberta, vertical shear is probably favorable for convection with some severe wind/hail in areas where instability becomes locally maximized late this afternoon. An isolated supercell may not be out of the question, with activity tending to develop northeastward across the mountains of southwest Montana and northeast Wyoming through late afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few marginally severe wind gusts remain possible for the next few hours across the region. A WW is not currently anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Widespread convection has developed within a confluent band along the northeast periphery of Tropical Depression Alberto. A few reports of tree damage were received along with sub-marginal wind gusts of up to 35-45 kts measured across southwest Ohio. Ample surface heating, with resultant 1000 J/kg MLCAPE currently reside ahead of the aforementioned convective band across portions of southern Michigan and and western/central Ohio. As such, a few more instances of gusty winds remain possible until diurnal cooling and subsequent stabilization set in. Given the isolated and marginal extent of the damaging wind threat, a WW issuance is not currently anticipated.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A marginal severe threat will be possible for a couple more hours across parts of eastern Colorado and northwest Kansas. Hail and strong wind gusts may occur but any severe threat is expected to remain too marginal for weather watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest surface analysis shows a 1002 mb low in southeast Colorado with upslope east-southeasterly flow across most of northeast Colorado. Thunderstorms are ongoing from near Limon, CO northeastward to Holyoke, CO. To the east of these storms, surface dewpoints are in the mid to upper 50s F and the RAP has about 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE. In addition, the Goodland WSR-88D VWP shows 0-6 km shear of 25 kt suggesting deep-layer shear is strong enough for a marginal severe threat. As the storms move eastward into an instability max near the CO-KS state line early this evening, hail and a few marginally severe wind gusts could accompany the stronger multicells. As instability decreases, the threat is expected to diminish during the 00Z to 01Z timeframe.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms ongoing in a line from southeast Colorado, far western Oklahoma Panhandle, and the along the northern border of New Mexico and the Texas Panhandle will move into an area of greater surface moisture and instability over the next few hours. Severe wind gust and hail threats will increase as this occurs.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Current surface analysis show a weak low pressure center in the far western Texas Panhandle with a dryline extending southeastward from DUX to CDS. A warm front is evident in the north Texas Panhandle eastward into northern Oklahoma. Storms have been ongoing in western portions of WW 134. Over the last hour or so, radar trends show that storms have taken on more of a linear mode. As these storms progress east, they will encounter a moist, unstable airmass characterized by mid- to upper-60s dewpoints and surface temperatures into the 90s. MLCAPE values will be anywhere from 2000 to 3500 J/kg. Storm severity is expected to increase in the next few hours. Some uncertainty exists as to the southern extent of this line of storms. Some signs of cumulus development have been evident on visible satellite imagery near DUX. Should further development occur, possible watch extensions in area may be needed along the southern edge of WW 134. ..Wendt.. 05/30/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A cluster of storms in the Oklahoma and far northern Texas Panhandles is expected to continue moving east and grow upscale with time. Severe wind gusts and isolated hail will be possible with these storms. A WW is likely by about 02Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of storms is ongoing in the Oklahoma and far northern Texas Panhandles. Per KAMA radar, the southern flank of this activity has seen a recent uptick in intensity. This uptick in activity is coincident with the cluster encountering a more favorable convective environment and downstream dewpoints range from the mid-60s to low-70s in Oklahoma. MLCAPE values range from 1500 to 3500 J/kg per mesoanalysis. Recent CAMs guidance also depicts more development on the southern flank. While storms currently remain semi-discrete, with time cold pools should congeal and a more linear mode will dominate. Upscale growth with further be aided by an increase in the LLJ within the next few hours. The greatest uncertainty with this activity is how far south the storms will push into Oklahoma. A WW will likely be issued by about 02Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat will likely continue late this evening into the overnight period across northern Oklahoma and southern Kansas. Large hail and wind damage will be possible as a line of storms moves eastward across WW 135. Additional counties may need to be added to the watch across parts of western and central Oklahoma.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest surface analysis shows a 999 mb low across northwest Texas with the moist sector wrapping around the low on the east side. Surface dewpoints increase with eastward extent reaching the mid 70s F across the central and eastern part of WW 135. In response, MLCAPE values are in the 2500 to 4000 J/kg range according to the RAP across the watch. This will help to sustain a linear MCS as it moves across northern Oklahoma and southern Kansas late this evening into the overnight period. The Vance, OK WSR-88D VWP shows moderate deep-layer shear and forecast soundings have steep mid-level lapse rates of 7.5 to 8.0 C/km. This will be favorable for large hail with the stronger cores of the linear MCS. Also, an eastward movement of the MCS in the 40 to 50 kt range will also be favorable for wind damage along the leading edge. Given the recent development near the Texas and Oklahoma state line, Roger Mills and Custer counties may need to be added to the watch. Canadian and Oklahoma counties may eventually need to be added depending upon how much development occurs along the southern flank of the MCS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Expecting a concentrated corridor of severe gusts (60-75 mph) near US 412 between 1am-2am CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a mature/severe squall line moving east at 45 kt across north-central OK. The 04Z OUN RAOB showed a very steep 700-500 mb lapse rate (8.6 degree C/km) and the KTLX VAD has shown a strengthening in the 0.5-1.0 km south-southwesterly flow from 35 to 45 kt. The Breckenridge, OK mesonet observed a 67 mph gust at 1240am CDT and other sub-severe gusts have been recorded to the north and south of the apex of the smaller-scale bow that moved over Breckenridge. The expectation is the strongest gusts will concentrate near the US 412 corridor over the next hour as the bow apex continues to surge eastward across this area. ..Smith.. 05/31/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong to severe gusts (50-65 mph) are possible over the next 1-2 hours over southeast KS and northeast OK. There is uncertainty whether an additional severe thunderstorm watch is needed farther east over southwest MO and extreme northwest AR. Short-term observational trends will be monitored and will likely dictate a go vs. no-go decision on a southwest MO/northwest AR watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a strong to severe squall line over southeast KS extending south-southwestward into the greater OKC area. The airmass ahead of the squall line over northeast OK/southeast KS is very moist with lower 70s degree F dewpoints. Surface observations indicate slightly less rich moisture generally east of a north-south line east of Springfield. Nonetheless, the 00Z SGF RAOB showed a moderately buoyant airmass (2400 J/kg MLCAPE) which has only gradually lessened since earlier this evening. With a well-developed MCV now evident in radar imagery and a pronounced pressure rise in the trailing stratiform region (5-6 mb pressure rise in 2 hours at Ponca City, OK), it seems very likely the squall line will persist longer and farther east than recent runs of the HRRR indicated. Yet, recent measured gusts on the OK Mesonet have only observed gusts ranging between 40-50 mph. As such, will monitor surface observation trends over the next 30-60 minutes to help decide whether an additional severe thunderstorm watch is warranted farther east.
